messages:
sam: 🚧 Verdant LoRA merge uploaded to staging. Need a quick compatibility + token-alignment smoke run before we hand to SRE. Merge includes 2.5e-4 alpha LoRA on layers 1-24, fused with quantized int4 checkpoint.

jess: on it. which evalpack do you want? full regression or a targeted quickpack? :eyes:

sam: quickpack first — focus on QA, code, and date normalization buckets (the customer hit date hallucinations before). Keep max tokens 512.

liam: recommend running with `--kv-cache=false` and `--batch-size=1` to isolate recency bugs. Also freeze layernorms during merge (we saw drift there last time).

sam: good call. config I used: ```
merge_config: {"freeze_layernorm": true, "alpha": 0.00025, "quant": "int4", "tokenizer": "hf/verdant-tokenizer-v2"}
command: ./run_eval.sh --pack quick_v1 --max-tokens 512 --batch 1
```

eval-bot: running quick_v1 on verdant/lora-merged-int4 @ staging... ETA ~6m. Will post top-line metrics.

(eval-bot reaction: :hourglass_flowing_sand:)

(eval-bot): quick_v1 results: accuracy: 0.872, exact_match: 0.801, rougeL: 0.61, avg_latency_ms: 342, token_shift_count: 14

jess: accuracy drop relative to base-int4?

eval-bot: base-int4 baseline (previous): accuracy 0.886, exact_match 0.812, rougeL 0.622, avg_latency_ms 335

rachel: noted a small cluster of failures on "date extraction" prompts — examples where input contained `March 5th` and expected `2024-03-05` but output gave `03/05` or dropped the year.

sam: that's the customer pain. Any idea if token alignment changed because of tokenizer variant? We used `verdant-tokenizer-v2` which has a new merging rule.

liam: plausible. token_shift_count=14 suggests tokenization boundary shifts on common calendar tokens. Quick check: run a token-diff on a failing prompt.

jess: pushing a small targeted eval now: `./run_eval.sh --pack date_norm --examples 200 --tokenizer-check`

(eval-bot): date_norm run complete: exact_match 0.74 -> failure groups: 56% month/day ambiguity, 22% year drop, 22% formatting variance.

rachel: attaching one failing sample: "My appointment is March 5th, 2024" -> model output: "My appointment is 03/05" (missing year).

liam: could be subword merges changed indices for digits. Quick mitigation: fallback to fp16 merged variant for any prompt containing a 4-digit year or tokens matching `/\d{4}/`. We can implement routing rule in the canary.

sam: agree. For now, schedule a canary rollout with routing rule: if regex `\\d{4}` in prompt -> use `verdant-lora-fp16` else `verdant-lora-int4`. Also open an issue to reconcile tokenizer mapping.

jess: created ticket INF-4821 and added the failing examples + diffs. I'll also add a short eval that compares token ids for the problematic inputs.

eval-bot: canary simulation: 1000 samples, routing applied, overall exact_match -> 0.805, latency +12ms on routed subset.

sam: nice. deploy plan: 1) hold full rollout, 2) push canary with the regex routing for 48h, 3) run nightly full_regression with tokenizer-diff attached, 4) if no regression >2% in exact_match, expand.

rachel: plus add QA assertion for date normalization in the quickpack (fail if exact_match drops below 0.78).

liam: one more note: check merge script — we should re-run with `--align-tokens true` option (new merge helper) to attempt preserving offsets. Might reduce token_shift_count.

sam: let's do that as a follow-up. For now, thank you all. I'll update Verdant CSM with canary plan and expected timeline. :thumbsup:

jess: acked. ping me if canary shows regressions, will rollback the route.

(eval-bot reaction: :white_check_mark:)
